notes:
Inbound SMB lead via self-serve signup. Came through trial signup on 2024-05-08.

Summary:
- Building a bot for transactional customer support (order status, returns) + KB search for help center. Small engineering team wants fast time-to-value.
- Interested in Hosted API only for now (no Dedicated/Private). Public cloud OK.
- Primary concern: what Redwood stores, for how long, and whether customers can opt-out of having prompts logged. Legal is risk-averse.

Key quotes / call snippets:
- "We need to be able to tell customers if their chat will be used for model training or logs retained." — Elise (Head of Product)
- "If a user requests deletion, how fast can you purge prompts from logs?" — Legal lead on call.

Specific retention questions flagged by legal/ops:
- What is default token/log retention window for Hosted API logs? Is it configurable per account?
- Is prompt text persisted in logs after anonymization? If so, for how long and where?
- Do you provide an explicit opt-out (no-store) API flag or header for requests that should not be recorded or used for improvement?
- Can Redwood provide an audit/trail that shows deletion occurred (for customer proof)?

What we demoed / materials shared:
- Quick walkthrough of Hosted API signup and keys (5/12). Fireflies: ff_3112_20240512.
- Shared pricing deck + short retention FAQ draft (links above).

Timeline / recent activity:

- 2024-05-11: initial intro email from Maya (owner) + schedule discovery call. Gmail thread: thread-CAJk3xYp_20240511.

- 2024-05-15: internal SE notes: need to confirm retention windows and opt-out header behavior. Created ticket INF-3421.
- 2024-05-18: follow-up meeting — legal requested written opt-out language and deletion SLA.

Technical/requirements notes (from SE):
- Latency: interactive chat, 95% requests < 600ms desired. Throughput low (10-60 rps).
- Cost sensitivity: high; evaluating token cost on longer context windows.
- Model preference: open models OK; prioritize Redwood-verified smaller models to reduce cost.
- Routing/fallback: want simple fallback to cheaper model if higher-latency model fails. Not required at sign-up.

Next steps (short):
- Deliver 1-page retention+opt-out FAQ (target 2024-05-20).
- Legal to review and confirm acceptable phrasing.
- If acceptable, coordinate a short POC using Hosted API no-store flag (demo ephemeral mode).

Notes about tone/likelihood:
- Lead is product-led but conservative on privacy; likely to convert if we give clear, short legal-friendly language and a demo of no-store behavior.
- Low ARR but good reference potential for SMB use-cases.
